result.topic_en: Draft passage stating that a trigonometric series can converge infinitely often in every interval even when its terms do not tend to zero, with an example built from a power series in q with q = e^{xi}, referring to Abel's theorem.
result.transcription:

methods.what: Construction of a trigonometric series as the imaginary part of a power series in q evaluated at q = e^{xi}
methods.quote: $\sum_{1,\infty} \frac{1}{n^3}(1-q^n)\log\left(\frac{-\log(1-q^n)}{q^n}\right)$, wo die Log. so zu nehmen sind, dass sie für $q=0$ verschwinden, nach steigenden Potenzen von q entwickelt, u. [-darin-] [-für-] $q=e^{xi}$ setzt

methods.what: Appeal to Abel's theorem on power series at the boundary of convergence

items.quote: In demselben Umfange, d. h. zwischen je zwei noch so nahen Argumentwerthen, unendlich [-oft-]{+oft+}, kann die trigonometrische Reihe auch {+selbst dann+} [-nicht-] convergiren, wenn ihre Glieder nicht {+zuletzt+} unendlich klein werden
items.english: To the same extent, i.e. infinitely often between any two argument values however close, the trigonometric series can converge even when its terms do not ultimately become infinitely small.

items.quote: so bildet [-...[?]-] [-...[?]-] [-dort[?]-] der imaginäre Theil eine trigonometrische Reihe, welche zweimal {+nach x+} differentiirt [-in jedem Intervalle-] {+in jedem Größenintervalle+} unendlich oft convergirt [-Werthe aber-], während ihr erster Differentialquotient unendlich oft unendlich wird.
items.english: Then the imaginary part forms a trigonometric series which, differentiated twice with respect to x, converges infinitely often in every interval, while its first derivative becomes infinite infinitely often.
